Hi Marcus / Lauren,

Thanks for the detailed notes and the attachments. We looked into the .ics and the issue is the way the series was created in Julie's calendar client. The .ics contains DTSTART entries without a TZID for the recurring instances and an X-WR-TIMEZONE header set to America/Los_Angeles, but our forwarding proxy (Bellwether's mail routing service) normalizes calendar items when forwarding through an EU-based system which strips the explicit TZID on recurrence rules. That makes some recipients' calendar clients treat instances as "floating."

Options we recommend (ordered by simplest to more-controlled):
1) Julie recreates the series and in the event settings selects the explicit timezone drop-down (America/Los_Angeles) rather than leaving the default. Attachments and metadata will then preserve TZID on DTSTART and RRULE instances.
2) Marcus or Lauren create the series on Redwood's calendar (America/Los_Angeles) and invite Bellwether directly — that avoids the forwarding proxy route.
3) Send the event as a single occurrence (no series) for the first meeting to confirm cross-region attendees, then convert to series once we verify it shows correctly.

We've tested with a sample forwarded invite and reproduced the floating behavior for recipients in Europe and India. Let us know which option you'd prefer and we can resend a corrected .ics.

Best,
Bellwether Calendar Support
calendar-support@bellwether.health
